---
title: "N-D Parallelism (Beta)"
---

Axolotl enables training models at scale by composing different parallelism techniques. This is essential when:

- A model's weights are too large to fit on a single GPU's memory.
- A model's activations, especially with very long contexts, are too large for a single GPU.
- You want to accelerate training by using multiple GPUs or nodes.

or combinations of the above!

## Core Concepts

Parallelism strategies can be combined. The key is understanding how each one divides the workload. PyTorch's `DeviceMesh` is the modern way to manage these combinations, creating a logical grid of your GPUs and assigning different parallel strategies to different dimensions of the grid.

### Data Parallelism {#sec-dp}

Data Parallelism focuses on splitting the global data batch across GPUs.

- Distributed Data Parallel (DDP): The classic approach. The full model is replicated on every GPU. Each GPU processes a different slice of the data batch. Gradients are then averaged across all GPUs after the backward pass to keep the models synchronized. This can substantially improve data throughput compared to single-device training, but requires that each GPU is able to hold the entire model, its gradients, and optimizer states.

- [Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP)](multi-gpu.qmd#fully-sharded-data-parallel-(fsdp)): A highly memory-efficient form of data parallelism (inspired by DeepSpeed's ZeRO). Instead of replicating the model, FSDP shards the model's *parameters, gradients, and optimizer states* across the GPUs in the data-parallel group. During computation, each GPU receives the specific parameters it needs via an `all_gather` operation just before they are used, and they can be discarded immediately after (`reshard-after-forward`).
    - FSDP maps to ZeRO stages:
        - ZeRO-2 (`reshard_after_forward=False`): Shards gradients and optimizer states. Model weights are replicated on each GPU.
        - ZeRO-3 (`reshard_after_forward=True`): Shards gradients, optimizer states, AND model parameters. This provides the most memory savings at the cost of more communication (re-gathering parameters for both forward and backward passes).

### [Experimental] Tensor Parallelism (TP) {#sec-tp}

Also known as "horizontal model parallelism," as described in the [Megatron-LM paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.08053.pdf). Instead of splitting the batch, TP splits the model's layers themselves across GPUs.

- How it works: For a linear layer `Y = XA`, the weight matrix `A` is split column-wise (`A = [A_1, A_2]`). The computation becomes `Y_1 = XA_1` and `Y_2 = XA_2`, which can happen in parallel on different GPUs. The final output `Y` is simply the concatenation of `Y_1` and `Y_2`. Check [this comment](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/10321#issuecomment-783543530) for more detailed info.
- Requirement: TP involves frequent, small communications within a forward/backward pass. It requires a very fast interconnect between GPUs (e.g., NVLink) and is typically not recommended across different nodes.
- Limits: full-parameter training, or LoRA on a native NVFP4 base (the `torchao_tp_lora` path). Adapters on a bf16 base are rejected at model load because PEFT sizes the LoRA factors from the already TP-sharded base weight, so each rank would train a different shard-local adapter. `fsdp_config.cpu_ram_efficient_loading` is turned off under TP (each rank loads its own shard directly; a rank-0-only load would leave the other ranks with zeros). Every TP rank takes part in the final `save_pretrained`, and the logged `grad_norm` is the global norm.

### Context Parallelism (CP) {#sec-cp}

Context Parallelism (CP; the term we use for what some frameworks call sequence parallelism, see the [guide](sequence_parallelism.qmd)) addresses the memory bottleneck from long sequences. The input sequence itself is split along the sequence length dimension and distributed across the GPUs of a `cp` group; every GPU in the group sees the same batch.

- How it works: If you have a sequence of 8192 tokens and a `context_parallel_size` of 4, each GPU will only handle a chunk of 2048 tokens.
- The Challenge: Attention is not local; every token needs to "attend to" every other token. Splitting the sequence breaks this.
- The Solution (Ringmaster): CP is built in via [axolotl-ringmaster](sequence_parallelism.qmd) and needs no `plugins:` entry. With `context_parallel.backend: auto` (the default) it prefers **Ulysses**, which all-to-alls the attention *heads* across the group so each GPU runs ordinary attention on a subset of heads over the full sequence, and covers any remainder of the CP degree with **Ring** attention (KV blocks passed around the group), a combination known as USP. Ulysses runs on SDPA or Flash Attention; Ring/USP training needs Flash Attention. Set `backend: ulysses`, `ring`, or `usp` (with `ulysses_size` / `ring_size`) to override.
- Previous releases implemented CP with `ring-flash-attention` under `sequence_parallel_degree`; that key is deprecated and maps to `context_parallel_size`, and `ring_attn_func` / `heads_k_stride` are ignored.
- **Mamba/SSM and linear-attention hybrids** (Nemotron-H, Falcon-H1, Granite MoE Hybrid, GDN/KDA): Ringmaster shards the recurrent layers too, passing state across ranks. See [Context Parallelism](sequence_parallelism.qmd) for requirements.

### Expert Parallelism (EP) {#sec-ep}

Expert Parallelism shards the experts of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model across GPUs. Each rank holds `num_experts / ep_size` experts; tokens are routed to the rank that owns the chosen expert via a token dispatch/combine collective.

- How it works: the EP plugin slices each `Experts` module's `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` along the experts dimension and replaces the dispatch/combine path with the chosen backend. Each rank sees a different batch (so EP is data-parallel for *data*) but holds different expert shards (model-parallel for *expert weights*).
- When to use: MoE training where the experts dominate the parameter count and don't fit under FSDP alone, or where you want to compose with FSDP on orthogonal mesh axes.
- Requires FSDP2 (`fsdp_version: 2` + `fsdp_config`) with `fsdp_config.state_dict_type: FULL_STATE_DICT`; EP under DDP or with a sharded state dict is rejected at config validation (a sharded checkpoint would keep only EP group 0's experts). Composes with FSDP, CP and HSDP: `dp_replicate_size × expert_parallel_size × dp_shard_size × context_parallel_size = world_size`. EP shards experts on the `ep` axis; the dense parameters FSDP-shard across every other axis; the expert slices FSDP-shard across the `dp_shard` and `cp` ranks of their EP group (both see different tokens, so expert gradients reduce over both), with `dp_replicate` as an outer replication dim under HSDP (with no `dp_shard`/`cp` axis each replica keeps its expert slices whole and the replicas reduce expert gradients with each other). When `expert_parallel_size` equals the world size (pure EP) the trainable experts stay whole on each rank. Full-parameter and LoRA (`lora_target_parameters` on the experts) training both work; the saved checkpoint or adapter carries every expert. EP × TP is not supported.
- Two dispatch backends, set with `expert_parallel_backend` (default `auto`): `deep_ep` uses the [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP) library's fused kernels (Ampere or Hopper, all-pairs NVLink/RDMA); `torch` dispatches over a plain `all_to_all_single` on the EP process group and runs on any NCCL/gloo fabric, including PCIe-only nodes with no NVLink. `auto` picks `deep_ep` when it's importable, else `torch`. See [Expert Parallelism Integration](custom_integrations.qmd#expert-parallelism-integration) for backend details, install steps, and the `torch` backend's checkpointing note.
- Checkpoints and resume: the mid-training checkpoint (`pytorch_model_fsdp.bin`, `optimizer.bin`) holds every expert and, for LoRA on the experts, every expert's adapter, together with their optimizer state (Adam `exp_avg` / `exp_avg_sq`). Each tensor is gathered across the `ep` axis when saving, and on resume each EP rank loads only its own experts. The files are the same size as a non-EP FSDP2 `FULL_STATE_DICT` checkpoint and use the same shapes as the final export. Earlier versions saved only EP group 0's experts (1/`ep_size` of them), so resuming gave every EP group group 0's experts. Resuming from a checkpoint written by those versions now fails with an error. Resume from a checkpoint saved by this version instead, or start a new run from the final export, which was always complete. For LoRA runs, the old checkpoint's `adapter_model.safetensors` is complete and can be loaded with `lora_model_dir`, but the optimizer state is lost. Each rank picks its experts out of the full tensors, so the files don't depend on the `ep` / `dp_shard` layout they were saved with. Resuming with a different `expert_parallel_size` should therefore work, but it is untested.

### Hybrid Sharding Data Parallel (HSDP) {#sec-hsdp}

HSDP is a 2D strategy that intelligently combines FSDP and DDP, typically for multi-node training.

- Intra-Node (within a machine): Use FSDP. This is efficient because GPUs on the same node have fast interconnects (NVLink), making the `all_gather` operations for sharded parameters fast.
- Inter-Node (across machines): Use DDP. The gradient synchronization between nodes is less frequent than FSDP's parameter gathering, making it a better fit for the slower node-to-node network (e.g., Ethernet/Infiniband).
- Example: With 2 nodes of 8 GPUs each (16 total), you could have `dp_shard_size=8` (FSDP within each node) and `dp_replicate_size=2` (DDP across the two nodes).

## Usage

```yaml
# FSDP config. See https://docs.axolotl.ai/docs/multi-gpu.html#sec-fsdp
fsdp_version: 2
fsdp_config:
  # ...

# The number of GPUs to shard the model parameters across (FSDP dimension).
dp_shard_size: 4

# The number of times to replicate the sharded model (DDP dimension).
dp_replicate_size: 2

# Number of GPUs for Tensor Parallelism.
tensor_parallel_size: 1  # (default is 1, no TP)

# Number of GPUs for Context Parallelism.
context_parallel_size: 1 # (default is 1, no CP)

# Number of GPUs to shard MoE experts across (Expert Parallel).
expert_parallel_size: 1  # (default is 1, no EP)
```

Note: We recommend FSDP. DeepSpeed is only compatible with `tensor_parallel_size`.

## Examples

::: {.callout-tip}
See our example configs [here](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/tree/main/examples/distributed-parallel).
:::

1.  HSDP on 2 nodes with 4 GPUs each (8 GPUs total):
    - You want FSDP within each node and DDP across nodes.
    - Set `dp_shard_size: 4` and `dp_replicate_size: 2`.

2.  FSDP + TP on a single 8-GPU node:
    - You want to split the model across 4 GPUs using FSDP, and further split each layer across 2 GPUs with TP.
    - Set `dp_shard_size: 4` and `tensor_parallel_size: 2`.

3.  FSDP + CP on a single 8-GPU node for long context:
    - You want to shard the model across all 8 GPUs and also split the sequence length across all 8 GPUs.
    - Set `dp_shard_size: 8` and `context_parallel_size: 8`. Note: this means the data parallel group and context parallel group are the same. A more common setup might be to shard across a smaller group.

4.  FSDP + EP on a 4-GPU MoE training run:
    - You want EP to shard the experts and FSDP to shard non-expert params on orthogonal mesh axes.
    - Set `expert_parallel_size: 2` and `dp_shard_size: 2` (`ep × dp_shard == world_size`).

5.  EP + CP on a 4-GPU long-context MoE run:
    - You want the experts sharded and each sequence split across 2 GPUs.
    - Set `expert_parallel_size: 2` and `context_parallel_size: 2`. Add `dp_shard_size: 2` on 8 GPUs to also shard the dense weights (`ep × cp × dp_shard == world_size`).
    - Axis order is `dp_replicate, dp_shard, cp, ep, tp` (outer to inner): `ep` groups are consecutive ranks and stay node-local whenever `ep × tp` fits on a node, while `dp_shard` groups stride across nodes. The startup log prints the mesh and which axes cross nodes.

6.  HSDP + EP on 2 nodes of 4 GPUs:
    - Set `dp_replicate_size: 2`, `expert_parallel_size: 2`, `dp_shard_size: 2`.

Minimal MoE configs for the two EP compositions (4 and 8 GPUs; everything else is an ordinary FSDP2 config):

```yaml
# EP x CP on 4 GPUs: experts sharded 2 ways, each sequence split across 2 GPUs
base_model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B
expert_parallel_size: 2
context_parallel_size: 2
fsdp_version: 2
fsdp_config:
  auto_wrap_policy: TRANSFORMER_BASED_WRAP
  transformer_layer_cls_to_wrap: Qwen3MoeDecoderLayer
  state_dict_type: FULL_STATE_DICT
  cpu_ram_efficient_loading: true
attn_implementation: flash_attention_2
sample_packing: false
```

```yaml
# HSDP x EP on 2 nodes x 4 GPUs: replicate across nodes, EP x FSDP inside each node
base_model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B
dp_replicate_size: 2
expert_parallel_size: 2
dp_shard_size: 2
fsdp_version: 2
fsdp_config:
  auto_wrap_policy: TRANSFORMER_BASED_WRAP
  transformer_layer_cls_to_wrap: Qwen3MoeDecoderLayer
  state_dict_type: FULL_STATE_DICT
  cpu_ram_efficient_loading: true
```

`expert_parallel_backend` defaults to `auto` (DeepEP when installed, else the torch all-to-all backend); LoRA on the experts works with `lora_target_parameters` in either layout. A fresh LoRA adapter is drawn per module from `seed`, so the init (and a one-step gradient check) is identical whether or not the experts are sharded.

## Support Matrix

This matrix describes how different parallelism methods can be combined in Axolotl.

| Combination | `dp_replicate_size` | `dp_shard_size` | `tp_size` | `cp_size` | `ep_size` | Status & Notes |
| --- | :---: | :---: |:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| **FSDP** (ZeRO-3) | 1 | >1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | ✅ Fully supported. Shards model across all GPUs. |
| **HSDP** | >1 | >1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | ✅ Fully supported. FSDP intra-node, DDP inter-node. |
| **FSDP + TP** | 1 | >1 | >1 | 1 | 1 | ✅ **2D Parallelism**. Shards the model across a `dp_shard` group, and TP-splits layers within the `tp` group. Verified on dense and MoE (grouped_mm) models against FSDP-only; full-parameter, or LoRA on native NVFP4 bases. |
| **HSDP + TP** | >1 | >1 | >1 | 1 | 1 | ⚠️ **3D Parallelism**. Same code path as FSDP + TP; not yet verified for parity. |
| **FSDP + CP** | 1 | >1 | 1 | >1 | 1 | ✅ **2D Parallelism**. Combines FSDP with context parallelism; gradients verified identical to plain FSDP at the same data-parallel degree (Ulysses, 8 GPUs). |
| **HSDP + CP** | >1 | >1 | 1 | >1 | 1 | ✅ **3D Parallelism**. Verified with FSDP + CP; needs `dp_shard_size > 1`. |
| **FSDP + TP + CP**| 1 | >1 | >1| >1| 1 | ⚠️ **3D Parallelism**. Same code path as FSDP + TP; not yet verified for parity. |
| **EP** | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | =world | ✅ Supported (MoE only). Shards experts across all ranks; dense weights FSDP-sharded across the world. Every EP layout requires FSDP2 with `state_dict_type: FULL_STATE_DICT`. |
| **FSDP + EP** | 1 | >1 | 1 | 1 | >1 | ✅ **2D Parallelism** (MoE). EP shards experts on the `ep` axis; FSDP shards non-experts on `dp_shard`. |
| **EP + CP** | 1 | 1 | 1 | >1 | >1 | ✅ **2D Parallelism** (MoE, long context). Experts on `ep`, sequences on `cp`; expert slices FSDP-shard across `cp`. |
| **FSDP + EP + CP** | 1 | >1 | 1 | >1 | >1 | ✅ **3D Parallelism** (MoE). Expert slices shard across `dp_shard × cp`. |
| **HSDP + EP** | >1 | >1 | 1 | 1 | >1 | ✅ **3D Parallelism** (MoE, multi-node). `dp_replicate` replicates the whole EP × FSDP layout; needs `dp_shard_size > 1` (or `cp_size > 1`, next row). |
| **HSDP + EP**, no shard axis | >1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | >1 | ✅ **2D Parallelism** (MoE, multi-node). `dp_replicate` replicates the pure-EP layout; the dense weights FSDP-shard over `ep` inside each replica and the expert slices stay whole per rank, reducing across replicas. |
| **HSDP + EP + CP** | >1 | 1 | 1 | >1 | >1 | ✅ **3D Parallelism** (MoE, multi-node, long context). `dp_replicate` outermost; the dense weights FSDP-shard over `ep × cp` and the expert slices over `cp`, so no `dp_shard` axis is needed (accelerate's own DDP + CP rejection is lifted when `ep` supplies the shard group). |
| EP + TP | 1 | * | >1 | * | >1 | ❌ Not supported; rejected at config validation. |
| DDP + TP/CP | >1 | 1 | >1 | >1 | 1 | ❌ **Not Supported**. The `ParallelismConfig` explicitly prevents this, as composing pure DDP with TP or CP is currently not supported. You should use FSDP + TP/CP instead (`dp_shard_size > 1`). |
| Just TP / CP | 1 | 1 | >1 | >1 | 1 | ✅ Supported. Useful for inference or when the model fits on one GPU but context is too long. |

::: {.callout-note}
Axolotl normalizes the loss per rank (`average_tokens_across_devices` is off), so without CP each rank's tokens are averaged separately and the ranks are then averaged. Under CP the count is the global one for the CP group, so the same batch is token-weighted slightly differently than an FSDP-only run with the same data-parallel degree. Both are valid mean losses; they only coincide when every rank holds the same number of supervised tokens.
:::

- `tp_size` refers to `tensor_parallel_size`
- `cp_size` refers to `context_parallel_size`
- `sp` is accelerate's DeepSpeed Ulysses axis; axolotl sets it only when `context_parallel_size` runs under `deepspeed:`. Older configs' `sequence_parallel_degree` is a deprecated alias of `context_parallel_size`.
- `ep_size` refers to `expert_parallel_size`
